html:
British Guiana was a British colony on the northern coast of South America, now the independent country of Guyana.

The Dutch settled this coast first, in the 1600s, and built the sugar colonies of Essequibo, Berbice and Demerara, shown on older maps as Dutch Guiana. Britain seized them in 1796 during its wars with France, handed them back, took them again in 1803 and kept them under the peace of 1814. In 1831 the three were joined as British Guiana. The English explorer Walter Raleigh had written of the region two centuries before, chasing tales of a city of gold.

Sugar ruled the colony. Enslaved Africans rose in the Demerara rebellion of 1823, and slavery ended with the Slavery Abolition Act in 1834. Planters then brought indentured workers, above all from India, who became the largest group in the colony. Britain and Venezuela quarrelled over the western border, settled in Britain's favour by an arbitration in 1899. Guyana became independent in 1966.
sum: British Guiana was a British colony on the northern coast of South America, now the independent country of Guyana.
